== APPRAISAL INSTRUCTIONS (GEMINI_HANDOFF_BRIEF §3 Task D; RISK_OF_BIAS.md §§1-2; APPRAISAL_FORM.md; CODEBOOK.md §8) ==
1. ACCESSIBILITY GATE:
   - If `Retrieval status` is `not_accessible` (or the paper text below says `[FULL TEXT NOT ACCESSIBLE]`), you MUST set `paper_read = "not accessible"`, `study_design_identified = "cannot_tell (full text not accessible)"`, `chosen_tool = "cannot_tell"`, `why_tool_chosen = "full text not accessible"`, `overall_rating = "cannot_tell"`, `domain_ratings = []`, all 7 `cross_tool_domains` fields to `"cannot_tell"`, `overall_narrative_summary = "Full text not accessible; no risk-of-bias appraisal performed."`, `where_found_summary = "not accessible"`, and `evidence_quotes = []`. NEVER guess study design or bias ratings from citation/title!

2. STEP 1 — INDEPENDENT DESIGN CLASSIFICATION & TOOL SELECTION (`RISK_OF_BIAS.md` §1):
   Classify the study's actual design from its Methods section, then select the matching appraisal tool:
   - `"RoB 2 (parallel-trial variant)"`: Individually randomized controlled trial. Rate all 5 domains (`D1` Randomization process; `D2` Deviations from intended interventions; `D3` Missing outcome data; `D4` Measurement of the outcome; `D5` Selection of the reported result) as `"Low"`, `"Some concerns"`, or `"High"`, and overall rating as `"Low"`, `"Some concerns"`, or `"High"`.
   - `"RoB 2 (cluster-randomized trials variant)"`: Cluster-randomized trial (villages, compounds, neighbourhoods, schools, utilities randomized as clusters). Rate all 6 domains (`D1a` Randomization process; `D1b` Timing of identification or recruitment of participants within clusters; `D2` Deviations from intended interventions; `D3` Missing outcome data; `D4` Measurement of the outcome; `D5` Selection of the reported result) as `"Low"`, `"Some concerns"`, or `"High"`, and overall rating as `"Low"`, `"Some concerns"`, or `"High"`.
   - `"ROBINS-I"`: Non-randomized study of an intervention / policy with a genuine comparator (DiD, IV, RDD, PSM, ITS, controlled before-after, comparative longitudinal/panel evaluation). Rate all 7 domains (`D1` Bias due to confounding; `D2` Bias in selection of participants into the study; `D3` Bias in classification of interventions; `D4` Bias due to deviations from intended interventions; `D5` Bias due to missing data; `D6` Bias in measurement of outcomes; `D7` Bias in selection of the reported result — note `No information` honestly if no pre-analysis plan/protocol exists) as `"Low"`, `"Moderate"`, `"Serious"`, `"Critical"`, or `"No information"`, and overall rating in the same vocabulary. Do NOT assign single-case histories with no comparator arm to ROBINS-I!
   - `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies"`: Quantitative cross-sectional survey / observational regression without a quasi-experimental intervention structure. Rate all 8 items (`Q1` Inclusion criteria in sample clearly defined; `Q2` Study subjects and setting described in detail; `Q3` Exposure measured validly and reliably; `Q4` Objective, standard criteria used for measurement of condition; `Q5` Confounding factors identified; `Q6` Strategies to deal with confounding factors stated; `Q7` Outcomes measured validly and reliably; `Q8` Appropriate statistical analysis used) as `"Yes"`, `"No"`, `"Unclear"`, or `"Not applicable"`. Provide overall narrative judgment (`"Low concern"`, `"Some concern"`, or `"High concern"` — no numeric score).
   - `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Cohort Studies"`: Observational comparative cohort design (not framed as a ROBINS-I intervention). Rate all 11 items (`Q1` Similar groups from same population; `Q2` Exposures measured similarly; `Q3` Exposure measured validly/reliably; `Q4` Confounding factors identified; `Q5` Strategies to deal with confounding stated; `Q6` Participants free of outcome at start; `Q7` Outcomes measured validly/reliably; `Q8` Follow-up time reported and sufficient; `Q9` Follow-up complete or loss explored; `Q10` Strategies to address incomplete follow-up utilized; `Q11` Appropriate statistical analysis used) as `"Yes"`, `"No"`, `"Unclear"`, or `"Not applicable"`, plus narrative overall judgment (`"Low concern"`, `"Some concern"`, `"High concern"`).
   - `"CASP Qualitative Checklist"`: Primary qualitative study (interviews, ethnography, focus groups, qualitative documentary/field case study). Rate all 10 items (`Q1` Clear statement of aims; `Q2` Qualitative methodology appropriate; `Q3` Research design appropriate to address aims; `Q4` Recruitment strategy appropriate to aims; `Q5` Data collected in a way that addressed research issue; `Q6` Relationship between researcher and participants adequately considered [reflexivity]; `Q7` Ethical issues considered; `Q8` Data analysis sufficiently rigorous; `Q9` Clear statement of findings; `Q10` How valuable is the research [narrative assessment]). Rate Q1-Q9 `"Yes"`, `"No"`, or `"Can't tell"`, and Q10 narratively; give narrative `overall_rating` (e.g. `"Low methodological concern"`, `"Moderate concern (X Can't tell / No items)"`, `"High methodological concern"` — no numeric score).
   - `"MMAT (Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool)"`: Genuine mixed-methods primary study combining qualitative AND quantitative empirical components (do NOT assign purely quantitative or purely qualitative studies to MMAT). Rate Screening `S1`-`S2`, Qualitative `1.1`-`1.5`, the matching Quantitative 5-item block (`2.1`-`2.5` randomized, `3.1`-`3.5` non-randomized, or `4.1`-`4.5` descriptive), AND Mixed-Methods integration `5.1`-`5.5` (`5.1` adequate rationale for mixed methods; `5.2` components effectively integrated; `5.3` outputs of integration adequately interpreted; `5.4` divergences/inconsistencies adequately addressed; `5.5` components adhere to quality criteria of each tradition) as `"Yes"`, `"No"`, or `"Can't tell"`. Per MMAT 2018 rules, NEVER compute a numeric score; provide a concise criterion-grounded narrative `overall_rating` noting that overall quality cannot exceed the weakest component.
   - `"AMSTAR 2"`: Secondary systematic review, meta-analysis, or scoping review with an explicit systematic search/screening method (NEVER apply AMSTAR 2 to non-systematic narrative literature reviews!). Rate all 16 items `Q1`-`Q16` (explicitly marking critical domains `Q2`, `Q4`, `Q7`, `Q9`, `Q11`, `Q13`, `Q15`) as `"Yes"`, `"Partial Yes"` (where applicable), `"No"`, or `"Not applicable (no meta-analysis)"`, and apply AMSTAR 2 overall confidence (`"High"`, `"Moderate"`, `"Low"`, `"Critically Low"`).
   - `"Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework"`: Doctrinal-empirical hybrid, jurimetric analysis, or institutional/legal-historical case study that fits NONE of the six conventional designs above. Rate all 13 narrative domains (`D1` Legal source accuracy; `D2` Jurisdictional specificity; `D3` Exposure definition; `D4` Outcome definition; `D5` Sampling transparency; `D6` Selection process; `D7` Measurement transparency; `D8` Causal identification; `D9` Treatment of confounding; `D10` Institutional context; `D11` Replication potential; `D12` Coding transparency; `D13` Researcher reflexivity) as `"strong"`, `"adequate"`, `"weak"`, or `"not assessable"`. Explicitly frame `overall_rating` as a structured non-validated judgment (NEVER a numeric composite score!).
   - `"NONE"`: Use when the study fits NONE of the listed instruments (e.g., pure mathematical/simulation optimization model with no empirical sample, or non-systematic narrative essay/review with no primary empirical method and no systematic search). Set `overall_rating = "NOT APPLICABLE (design fits no listed tool)"`, explain clearly in `why_tool_chosen` and `overall_narrative_summary` rather than forcing an inappropriate checklist, and still fill the 7 `cross_tool_domains` honestly from the paper!

cross_tool_domains.attrition: Not applicable at the participant level (secondary systematic review with no primary cohort follow-up); however, at the study-selection pipeline level, the 4 excluded records out of 24 unique studies are not bibliographically identified, and record-tracking totals conflict between Section 3.5 (62 records -> 24 unique) and Section 4 (62 database + 8 citation-search = 70 records -> 24 unique -> 4 excluded = 20 included).
cross_tool_domains.confounding: High concern — Because no risk-of-bias or causal-identification appraisal was conducted on the 20 included studies, the review treats observational associations and descriptive policy claims regarding Jal Jeevan Mission (e.g., reductions in waterborne diseases, women's time reallocation, and haemoglobin levels) as direct programme impacts without accounting for confounding or baseline secular trends in the underlying studies.
cross_tool_domains.legal_measurement_quality: Weak — Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) is framed generically as a national flagship programme targeting universal Functional Household Tap Connections (FHTCs) and decentralized Gram Panchayat participation, without operationalizing or verifying statutory mandates, official JJM operational guidelines, intergovernmental fiscal rules, or binding service-level standards across jurisdictions.
cross_tool_domains.measurement_bias: High concern — Data extraction was not performed independently in duplicate (Author Contributions p. 13 attributes data collection to a single author, with NVivo coding merely reviewed by co-authors, Section 4.1), per-study characteristics/sample sizes/outcomes were omitted from Table 1, no validated risk-of-bias tool was used (Section 3.9), and citation-mapping errors occur in Table 1 (both item 4 'Ranjeet Kumar' and item 10 'Kumar & Goyal' cite reference [9]).
cross_tool_domains.outcome_measurement_quality: Weak — Rural drinking water, health, socio-economic, and local governance outcomes are synthesized solely as broad qualitative themes without extracting standardized outcome definitions, tap functionality metrics, microbiological/chemical water-quality indicators, or quantitative effect sizes from the 20 reviewed papers.
cross_tool_domains.reporting_bias: High concern — No a priori protocol or registration exists (AMSTAR 2 Q2 = No); English-only restrictions and exclusion of grey literature were acknowledged only post hoc as limitations (Section 8); study-level details promised in Section 5 (publication year, sampling, sample size) do not appear in Table 1; and unscreened external references ([25], [26], [31], [32]) are introduced into the thematic findings and conclusion.
cross_tool_domains.selection_bias: High concern — Despite reporting independent title/abstract screening (Section 3.1), the review capped Google Scholar retrieval at an arbitrary 20 articles (Section 3.6), excluded regional-language and grey literature without methodological justification, provided no list of excluded full-text studies, and included a 2019 study from Kenya (Agesa & Agesa [13], Table 1 item 8) despite eligibility criteria requiring focus on India's Jal Jeevan Mission.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Did the research questions and inclusion criteria for the review include the components of PICO?
domain_ratings.justification: Objectives (Section 2.1) and eligibility criteria (Sections 3.1, 3.7) specify a broad policy topic (Jal Jeevan Mission and rural drinking water in India) and thematic outcomes, but do not formulate structured PICO components (no defined comparator group or operationalized population/outcome eligibility thresholds).

domain_ratings.domain_name: [CRITICAL] Did the report of the review contain an explicit statement that the review methods were established prior to the conduct of the review and did the report justify any significant deviations from the protocol?
domain_ratings.justification: No pre-registered or pre-established written protocol (e.g., PROSPERO or OSF registration) is mentioned anywhere in the manuscript, nor are protocol deviations addressed; Section 2.2 merely states that a systematic review analysis was adopted.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Did the review authors explain their selection of the study designs for inclusion in the review?
domain_ratings.justification: Section 3.4 states that scholarly articles, review papers, and book chapters were included, and Section 3.7 excludes works lacking 'empirical or analytical insights', but no methodological rationale is provided for selecting and pooling diverse primary qualitative, survey, and secondary review/commentary designs.

domain_ratings.domain_name: [CRITICAL] Did the review authors use a comprehensive literature search strategy?
domain_ratings.justification: Although multiple databases (Google Scholar, Scopus, ScienceDirect, Sage, Taylor & Francis, DOAJ, Elsevier, ResearchGate) and keywords plus backward/forward citation searching were used, the authors failed to justify the English-only restriction, excluded grey literature and registries, reported no reproducible database-specific Boolean strings, imposed an arbitrary 20-article stopping rule on Google Scholar (Section 3.6), and chose an unexplained 2002-2025 window for a programme launched in 2019. Under AMSTAR 2, failure to justify publication/language restrictions precludes even a Partial Yes.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Did the review authors perform study selection in duplicate?
domain_ratings.justification: Section 3.1 explicitly reports that retrieved records were screened independently by the authors based on titles and abstracts using predefined criteria, followed by full-text eligibility assessment with disagreements resolved through discussion (though inter-rater agreement statistics are not reported and Author Contributions on p. 13 attributes data collection to a single author).
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF Pages 3-4, Section 3.1; PDF Page 5, Section 3.8; PDF Pages 13-14, Author contributions

domain_ratings.domain_name: Did the review authors perform data extraction in duplicate?
domain_ratings.justification: No independent duplicate data extraction of study characteristics and findings is reported. Author Contributions (p. 13) states that data collection and analysis were performed by Malini Srinivasan, while Section 4.1 indicates only that NVivo thematic coding was subsequently 'reviewed by all the authors'.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF Pages 5-6, Sections 4 and 4.1; PDF Pages 13-14, Author contributions

domain_ratings.domain_name: [CRITICAL] Did the review authors provide a list of excluded studies and justify the exclusions?
domain_ratings.justification: Four studies were excluded during screening/full-text eligibility assessment (Sections 3.5 and 4), but no bibliographic list of excluded full-text studies or study-specific exclusion justifications is provided anywhere in the text or references.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Did the review authors describe the included studies in adequate detail?
domain_ratings.justification: Table 1 (p. 7) lists only serial numbers, author names, and article titles for the 20 included studies. Study-by-study descriptions of populations, sample sizes, settings, interventions, comparators, outcomes, and designs are entirely absent (despite Section 5 claiming results were presented by publication year, sampling, and sample size); Table 1 also contains citation errors (items 4 and 10 both map to reference [9]) and an out-of-scope Kenyan study (Agesa & Agesa [13]).

domain_ratings.domain_name: [CRITICAL] Did the review authors use a satisfactory technique for assessing the risk of bias (RoB) in individual studies that were included in the review?
domain_ratings.justification: No validated risk-of-bias or critical appraisal instrument was used. Section 3.9 ('Criteria for quality assessment and procedures') states only that full-text articles were read thoroughly by the three authors and that items published in 'reliable and reputed scholarly journals and books' were included, with zero evaluation of confounding, selection bias, measurement bias, or selective reporting in individual studies.
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF Page 3, Section 2.2; PDF Page 5, Section 3.9

domain_ratings.domain_name: Did the review authors report on the sources of funding for the studies included in the review?
domain_ratings.justification: The review reports its own ICSSR grant (pp. 13-14) but provides no information on funding sources or sponsorship of any of the 20 included studies.

domain_ratings.domain_name: [CRITICAL] If meta-analysis was performed did the review authors use appropriate methods for statistical combination of results?
domain_ratings.justification: No meta-analysis or quantitative pooling was performed; the review conducted qualitative thematic synthesis in NVivo 12 alongside descriptive counts of study approaches and methods.

domain_ratings.domain_name: If meta-analysis was performed, did the review authors assess the potential impact of RoB in individual studies on the results of the meta-analysis or other evidence synthesis?
[CRITICAL] Did the review authors account for RoB in individual studies when interpreting/ discussing the results of the review?
domain_ratings.justification: Because no valid risk-of-bias assessment was undertaken, the thematic synthesis and conclusions (Sections 6-7) treat findings from observational surveys, small case studies, and unvetted secondary commentaries as established causal impacts of JJM without weighting or qualifying conclusions by methodological quality or risk of bias.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Did the review authors provide a satisfactory explanation for, and discussion of, any heterogeneity observed in the results of the review?
domain_ratings.justification: While the authors note geographic variation in JJM implementation across drought-prone and groundwater-dependent regions (Sections 6.3, 6.6, 7), they do not investigate or explain how heterogeneity in study designs (6 quantitative, 11 qualitative, 3 mixed-methods, plus secondary reviews) affects reported outcomes, and they conflate evidence from the 20 screened studies with unscreened external citations ([25], [26], [31], [32]) in the thematic synthesis and conclusion.

domain_ratings.domain_name: [CRITICAL] If they performed quantitative synthesis did the review authors carry out an adequate investigation of publication bias (small study bias) and discuss its likely impact on the results of the review?
domain_ratings.justification: No quantitative synthesis or meta-analysis was performed (exclusion of grey literature and non-English studies is briefly noted only as a narrative limitation in Section 8).
domain_ratings.where_found: PDF Page 6, Section 4.1; PDF Page 13, Section 8

domain_ratings.domain_name: Did the review authors report any potential sources of conflict of interest, including any funding they received for conducting the review?
domain_ratings.justification: The authors explicitly disclose grant support from the Indian Council of Social Science Research (ICSSR), New Delhi, and declare that they have no competing interests.

raw_response.overall_narrative_summary: Under AMSTAR 2, confidence in the results of this systematic literature review (Ilangovan et al., 2026) is Critically Low due to five critical methodological flaws (Q2, Q4, Q7, Q9, Q13) alongside six non-critical weaknesses (Q1, Q3, Q6, Q8, Q10, Q14). Specifically, the review had no pre-registered or written a priori protocol (Q2); used a flawed search strategy that left English-only and grey-literature exclusions unjustified, omitted full Boolean search strings, and capped Google Scholar results at 20 articles (Q4); provided no list of the 4 excluded full-text studies with study-specific reasons (Q7); conducted no formal risk-of-bias appraisal of the 20 included studies beyond asserting they came from 'reliable and reputed scholarly journals and books' (Q9); and failed to account for primary-study risk of bias when interpreting causal claims regarding health and socio-economic impacts of India's Jal Jeevan Mission (Q13). In addition, study-level characteristics (population, sample size, design, outcomes) are omitted from Table 1 (Q8), duplicate data extraction was not performed (Q6), and severe internal reporting inconsistencies appear across the text—including record-count discrepancies between Section 3.5 (62 identified) and Section 4 (70 identified), duplicate mapping of two different studies in Table 1 to Reference [9], inclusion of a 2019 Kenyan study (Agesa & Agesa [13]) despite JJM-focused eligibility criteria, and incorporation of unscreened references ([25], [26], [31], [32]) into the thematic results and conclusion.
raw_response.study_design_identified: Systematic literature review (qualitative thematic synthesis of 20 included studies following PRISMA 2020, without meta-analysis)
raw_response.where_found_summary: Methods and search/screening procedures in Sections 2-4 (PDF Pages 2-6); study inventory and method counts in Section 5 / Tables 1-3 (PDF Pages 6-8); thematic synthesis and policy conclusions in Sections 6-7 (PDF Pages 8-13); limitations, author contributions, funding, and conflict-of-interest declarations in Section 8 and Declarations (PDF Pages 13-14).
raw_response.why_tool_chosen: The paper explicitly designs and executes a secondary Systematic Literature Review (SLR) under PRISMA 2020 guidelines with multi-database searching, backward/forward citation chasing, two-stage eligibility screening, a PRISMA flow process yielding 20 included studies, and NVivo 12 thematic synthesis. Per RISK_OF_BIAS.md §1, AMSTAR 2 is the mandatory instrument for systematic reviews with an explicit search and screening process.
